Definition: from G1223 and G5021; to arrange thoroughly, i.e. (specially) institute, prescribe, etc.:--appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.
BiblicalUsage: To appoint is to set in order, to arrange a thing as it should be, and Paul uses the word for the ordering of the churches. John tells the publicans to exact no more than is appointed them, the apostles appoint elders in every city, and the collection for the saints is appointed to be gathered on the first day of the week.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe appointing is how the church stays a church. Elders are appointed, collections are ordered, and the work is arranged so that nothing is left to chance and no one is left to carry it alone.
